title: Swiss Rösti (Golden Potato Cake)
summary: The traditional Swiss rösti: potatoes boiled whole and chilled overnight, then grated and fried into one large crisp-shelled cake, flipped halfway through to crisp both sides.
equipment: non-stick or cast-iron frying pan (25 cm)
flat plate larger than the pan

ingredients.item: waxy or all-purpose potatoes (such as Charlotte or Yukon Gold), unpeeled
fine salt, for the cooking water
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Boil the Potatoes Whole
steps.text: A day ahead, cover the whole unpeeled potatoes with cold water, add the salt, bring to a simmer and cook for 20-25 minutes, until a knife just pierces them but they're still firm. Try not to let the skins split, as that lets too much water in.

steps.title: Chill Overnight
steps.text: Drain, cool, then refrigerate overnight, uncovered after the first hour. Chilling sets the starch inside, which is what lets the grated shreds hold their shape in the pan rather than turning gluey.

steps.title: Peel and Grate
steps.text: Peel the cold potatoes and grate them on the large holes of the box grater. Season with the salt and pepper and mix gently with a fork, keeping the strands as intact as possible.

steps.title: Shape the Cake
steps.text: Melt half the butter in the frying pan over medium-high heat until foaming, then add the grated potato, pressing it into an even 2-3 cm cake and tucking in the edges.

steps.title: Cook the First Side
steps.text: Cook for 10-12 minutes, shaking the pan now and then, until the base is deep golden and crisp. The shaking helps the cake cook evenly without needing to lift and check it constantly.

steps.title: Flip and Finish
steps.text: Slide the rösti onto the plate, invert the pan over it and flip it back in. Add the remaining butter around the edge and cook for a further 10 minutes until golden, then cut into wedges and serve.

tips: Common mistake: grating warm or freshly boiled potatoes — without the overnight chill the starch hasn't set, so the shreds turn mushy and won't hold together in the pan.
Don't let the potatoes boil so long that the skins split; just-firm is exactly what you want before chilling.
Press the grated potato into a firm, even cake before cooking, as a loose pile won't hold together when flipped.
Shake the pan occasionally rather than lifting the rösti to check underneath, which can tear the forming crust.
Use a plate wider than the pan for flipping, so the whole cake lands safely without sliding off the edge.
storage: Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat well in a hot dry pan, both sides, until piping hot (74°C) and crisp again. Freezing isn't recommended, as the texture turns watery and soft once thawed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
